mcp.description: Connect Identity, Messaging, Payments, Vault and Lambda to your AI assistant through the Model Context Protocol and let it work with them directly.

identity.title: Authentication your users trust, without building it yourself.
identity.subtitle: Sign-up, login, sessions, two-factor, social sign-in and API keys in one service, with every application fully isolated.

login.title: E-mail and password, done right
login.description: Sign-up with e-mail verification, passwords hashed with argon2id, disposable e-mail addresses blocked and brute-force protection from the first request.

social.title: Social sign-in
social.description: Let people sign in with the account they already have. PKCE is mandatory between your app and Identity.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.description: Authenticator apps (TOTP) plus 10 single-use recovery codes. Choose per application how it works.

keys.title: Public and secret API keys
keys.description: Public keys for your frontend, secret keys for your backend. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored, and every key can be revoked or rotated.

privacy.title: Privacy and audit
privacy.description: Export or erase any user’s data with a single call (LGPD) and keep an immutable log of every sensitive action.

hero.title: Identity for your app, without reinventing authentication.
hero.subtitle: Sign-up, login, social sign-in, 2FA and access keys in one service. Every application isolated, every action recorded, and SDKs for every stack.

stats.label: Identity in numbers
stats.s4Label: export and erase any user’s data

caps.title: Everything your product’s authentication needs.
caps.subtitle: From sign-up to the right to be forgotten, every piece is ready and isolated per application.

c1.title: E-mail and password
c1.text: Sign-up with e-mail verification and protection against mass attempts. Nobody can find out who has an account in your app.

c2.title: Sessions
c2.text: Secure sessions that renew themselves and can be ended at any time, on one device or on all of them.

c3.title: Social sign-in
c3.text: Google, GitHub, Apple, Facebook and X. Your users sign in with the account they already have, and you enable only the providers you want.

c4.title: Two-factor (2FA)
c4.text: Two-factor authentication with an authenticator app and recovery codes. You decide, per application, how it works.

c5.title: API keys
c5.text: Public keys for your frontend and secret keys for your backend, with rotation that never breaks the integration.

c6.title: Roles
c6.text: Define who is an admin, who is a user and create whatever roles your product needs.

c7.title: Verification and reset
c7.text: Ready-made verification and password reset e-mails, with expiring codes that never reveal whether an account exists.

c8.title: Audit
c8.text: An immutable history of everything sensitive: logins, failures, role changes, keys and sessions.

c9.title: Privacy and LGPD
c9.text: Export or erase a user’s data with one call, and ban or unban accounts whenever you need to.

providers.title: Sign in with the account people already have.
providers.subtitle: Enable each provider per application, with your own credentials or Murkio’s. An existing account is never taken over on its own: the owner is notified and links the provider after signing in.

how.title: From the first sign-up to a valid session, in four steps.
how.subtitle: You choose what the application accepts and Identity handles the rest.
how.s1Text: Every application is born isolated, with default roles, configuration with history and a pair of keys, public and secret.
how.s2Text: Use the package for your language. It reads the application’s configuration and draws the published login screen.
how.s3Text: Sign-up, password, social sign-in or 2FA all end in a session ready to use.
how.s4Text: The SDK checks the session without overloading your API, and you can check on the spot when you need immediate revocation.

sec.title: Secure by default, from the first request.
sec.subtitle: No setting up protection later: it comes switched on.
sec.i1Text: Stored with modern algorithms, never in plain text, and upgraded automatically when the standard evolves.
sec.i2Text: Keys, tokens and codes are not readable, not even by us. Whatever must be recovered is encrypted.
sec.i3Text: One application’s data never shows up in another, and automated tests check it.
sec.i4Text: Excessive attempts are blocked and mass attacks trigger alerts.
sec.i5Text: Login, sign-up and reset answer the same, whether the account exists or not.
sec.i6Text: If a used token is presented again, the whole session ends immediately.

canvas.title: Design the login screen in the dashboard and publish it to the SDKs.
canvas.subtitle: The design of your site’s login and sign-up screen, built in the dashboard editor. The SDKs show the published version, so you never write the form.

mcp.title: Set everything up with AI, no account needed.
mcp.subtitle: Identity has its own MCP. Connect your AI assistant and ask for what you need: it builds everything for you.
mcp.p1: Create an application with e-mail and Google login.
mcp.p3: Generate the keys and show me the integration code in Go.
mcp.p4: Export the data of user ana@example.com.
mcp.connectText: Add the server to your assistant and you’re done.

faq.title: Common questions about Identity.
faq.a1: Each application has its own keys, users, roles and configuration. A user in one application never sees another’s data.
faq.q2: How do I validate the user in my backend?
faq.a2: The SDK checks the session for you, without a call to Identity on every request. When you need immediate revocation, you can check on the spot.
faq.q3: Can I use social sign-in only?
faq.a3: Yes. Password login can be turned off in the application’s configuration, and you enable only the providers you want.
faq.a4: You choose per application: off, optional or required. When required, users without an authenticator enroll one before signing in.
faq.a5: You are the controller and Murkio is the processor. Identity exports a user’s data, erases it effectively on request and keeps the audit history.
faq.a6: Not yet. They are in the works for TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Go, React, Svelte, Kotlin, Swift, Elixir, Ruby, PHP and C#.
faq.a7: Yes. Just add the Identity MCP server to your AI assistant and ask for what you need, no account required.

vault.title: Secrets without .env files.
vault.description: Store, reference and rotate every secret from one place, with an alert the moment one leaks.
vault.panelTitle: One URI and one token. Nothing else to ship.
vault.panelText: Manage every variable in a simple table in your panel. Your app fetches them at runtime, so there is no .env file to commit, leak or pass around the team.

feat.d1: Database URLs, JWT and PASETO keys and tokens, each with its own type and rules.
feat.d2: Rotate secrets on a schedule, or right away when a leak is detected.
feat.d3: Get notified in your panel if a secret is printed to the console or its URI shows up online.

payments.title: Receive, route and hold in one place.
payments.subtitle: Route payments between Stripe, AbacatePay, Asaas and Mercado Pago, keep the money in a single balance and, soon, spend it with a Murkio card.

card.title: Murkio card
card.description: Get a card for your balance, just like a digital bank.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: Keep your balance in one place, including some cryptocurrencies, with every movement tracked.

fraud.title: Fraud analysis built in
fraud.description: Every payment goes through Secure analysis before it is approved.

statement.title: Payments built for modern software.
statement.description: One API to charge, receive and hold money, from the first sale to the thousandth.

usage.title: Usage-based billing
usage.description: Usage from your applications is metered and billed automatically, so you only pay for what you use.

router.title: One router, every payment provider.
router.subtitle: Murkio routes each payment between Stripe, AbacatePay, Asaas and Mercado Pago, and keeps the money in a single balance.

balance.title: One balance, centralized in Murkio
balance.description: Whichever provider processes the payment, the money lands in a single Murkio balance, so you track everything in one place.

alert.title: Withdrawals depend on the providers
alert.description: The balance is centralized in Murkio, but withdrawal timelines and rules follow each provider: Stripe, AbacatePay, Asaas and Mercado Pago.

messaging.title: Every message, on the right channel.
messaging.subtitle: E-mail, in-app and push notifications from one place. Say which user should know about which event, and Murkio picks the channels.

code.title: One call, every channel
code.description: No addresses needed. Murkio picks the channels from the template, skips what the user turned off and delivers to each of their devices.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Email is guaranteed. SMS, WhatsApp, and Telegram are on the way.

templates.title: Templates by app, channel and language
templates.description: Write each message once per channel and language. When a language is missing, Murkio falls back to your app’s default.

prefs.title: Preferences your users control
prefs.description: Users choose by category and channel. Security and transactional messages can never be turned off.

inbox.title: A real-time inbox
inbox.description: An in-app inbox for every user, updated live as new messages arrive.
inbox.n2: New sign-in on a new device

lambda.title: Your scripts, running on their own.
lambda.subtitle: Write a Worker() function in your language and choose when it runs: on a timer or on a trigger. Made for the routine jobs that keep your database clean.

how.b1Text: Create a function called Worker() in your own language. It runs the job and returns nothing.
how.b2Text: Set the type in the worker’s panel: a timer, to run on a schedule, or a trigger, to run when an event happens.
how.b3Text: Delete expired sessions, archive old records, remove orphan files: the routine jobs that keep a database healthy.
